_comment: Out-of-sample STATE LEGISLATIVE reform validation: parametric state bills encoded in the PolicyEngine state-legislative-tracker, scored on the dataset as the change in the state's income tax (reform - baseline) and compared to the state's official fiscal note. State income-tax variables are defined_for their state, so the national delta IS the state delta. None of these are calibration targets. Fiscal notes score fiscal-year cash receipts while the simulation is calendar-tax-year liability, so timing gaps analogous to the JCT FY comparisons apply; each benchmark's window records what the figure covers. Bills whose official note is unpublished or whose parameters no longer exist upstream (SC H4216 contrib) are excluded.

source.note: reform_params from the tracker's reform_impacts table; official scores from state fiscal notes cited per row.

reforms.name: GA HB1001 — income tax rate cut (5.19% → 4.99%)
reforms.description: Georgia's 5.19%→4.99% flat-rate cut for 2026 (HB1001; enacted via HB463, so it is already in the policyengine-us baseline). Validated as a counterfactual revert to 5.19%. Benchmark is the DOAA fiscal note's individual-income-tax line, FY2028 -$680M (first year without withholding-refund timing; FY2029-31 grow -$712M→-$780M). The often-quoted ~$778M OPB budget figure includes ~$108-117M of corporate income tax, which the simulation's ga_income_tax measure excludes. Baseline nuance: current law reaches 4.99% by TY2030 via conditional cuts, so out-year figures depend on baseline choice.

benchmark.window: FY2028 (first clean full-cut year, individual income tax only)
benchmark.source: Georgia DOAA/OPB revised fiscal note, HB1001 (LC 59 0226-EC), Feb 24 2026

reforms.name: MD HB411 — standard deduction increase
reforms.description: Raises Maryland's standard deduction to $4,100/$8,200 in TY2026 with COLA thereafter (one-shot increase, no phase-in). DLS: -$149.6M GF in FY2027, but that fiscal year reflects TY2026 plus a portion of TY2027 (catch-up); the annualized FY2028 figure -$115.2M is the like-for-like for a single-tax-year simulation. The separate -$88.2M FY2027 local income tax impact is excluded (md_income_tax is state-only, verified).

benchmark.window: FY2028 (annualized single tax year, state GF)
benchmark.source: Maryland DLS fiscal note (First Reader, Feb 11 2026)

reforms.name: CO HB1062 — retirement income deduction expansion
reforms.description: Removes the cap on Colorado's pension/annuity subtraction. LCS: -$530M gross deduction impact TY2027 (-$565M steady state). Bill was postponed indefinitely; the fiscal note remains a valid benchmark.

benchmark.source: Colorado Legislative Council Staff fiscal note

reforms.name: ND HB1388 — marriage penalty elimination
reforms.description: Widens joint brackets to 2× single and repeals the marriage-penalty credit. Fiscal note: -$40.557M per biennium (bracket widening -$55.0M, credit repeal +$16.5M).

benchmark.source: ND Office of State Tax Commissioner fiscal note

reforms.name: IA HF1020 — child and dependent care credit expansion
reforms.description: Expands Iowa's CDCC fractions for higher income brackets. LSA: -$17.7M FY2026, -$16.2M FY2027; ~78,000 taxpayers affected, average decrease $228.

reforms.name: OK SB2156 — income tax elimination
reforms.description: Eliminates Oklahoma's personal income tax rates in 2026. OTC tax-year table: TY2026 -$4.947B, TY2027 -$5.202B, TY2028 -$5.445B (fiscal-year rows -$7.03B FY2027 with withholding timing, -$5.30B FY2028). Benchmark is the TY2026 line, matching the simulation period. Scope: total individual income tax including off-the-top apportionments — correct all-funds comparison for ok_income_tax. Static.

benchmark.source: Oklahoma Tax Commission revenue impact statement, Feb 10 2026

reforms.name: MI HB4170 — flat rate cut (4.25% → 4.05%)
reforms.description: Cuts Michigan's flat income tax rate by 0.20pp. HFA: ~$700M+/yr; 2023's actual revenue loss at 4.05% was ~$714M.

reforms.name: CA AB2591 — standard deduction increase
reforms.description: Raises California's standard deduction (contrib ab2591 module). FTB: -$7.0B/yr first full year, -$3.9B partial FY2026-27.

benchmark.source: CA FTB bill analysis (Feb 20 2026), explicitly static

reforms.name: KS HB2620 — EITC match 17% → 18%
reforms.description: One-point state EITC match increase (17%->18% of federal), TY2026. Fiscal note basis: $80.5M claimed at 17% in TY2024, scaled with IRS credit-amount growth; FY2027 -$5.0M SGF (captures TY2026), growing ~2.5%/yr. First match-change (not repeal) EITC validation row. Bill died in House Taxation without a hearing; the fiscal note stands regardless.

benchmark.source: Kansas Division of the Budget fiscal note on HB2620 (2/19/2026), incorporating KDOR estimate

reforms.name: KS HB2629 — standard deduction base increase
reforms.description: Raises the base standard deduction to $3,805 single / $8,640 joint / $6,480 HoH for TY2026. Benchmark is KDOR's single-tax-year liability simulation (-$10.4M on TY2024 data); the headline FY2027 figure (-$13.8M) blends TY2026 with 30% of TY2027 withholding and is NOT the comparator. SEPARATE/SURVIVING_SPOUSE amounts follow statutory ratios.

benchmark.source: Kansas Division of the Budget fiscal note on HB2629 (2/20/2026): KDOR simulation on TY2024 return data

reforms.name: ID SB1450 — $205/child CTC made permanent
reforms.description: Removes the 1/1/2026 sunset on Idaho's $205 nonrefundable per-child credit. The SOP frames it as no impact vs the DFM forecast (which assumed continuation) and puts the standalone cost at $63-65M/yr, with general-fund revenue rising ~$66M in FY2027 absent extension - the extension-cost benchmark used here. Sponsor-drafted range, not an independent fiscal-office point estimate.

benchmark.source: Idaho S1450 Statement of Purpose / Fiscal Note RS33273 (sponsor-prepared under Joint Rule 18)

reforms.name: CT SB69 — EITC repeal (40% of federal)
reforms.description: Eliminates the CT EITC (40% federal match + qualifying-child bonus). SB69 was a Proposed Bill with no fiscal note (OFA only scores bills reported out of committee); the benchmark is OFA's own tax-expenditure repeal figure - fiscal-year expenditure basis, static.

benchmark.source: CT OFA Connecticut Tax Expenditure Report, February 2026, summary table p.5 (detail p.37): EITC revenue gain in FY27 if repealed

reforms.name: CT HB5134 — new $600/child refundable CTC
reforms.description: Refundable $600/child CTC (max 3 children), AGI under $100k single / $200k joint. HB5134 itself (a Proposed Bill) has no fiscal note; OFA scored the same credit design in sSB-6 sec. 1 at -$316M/yr from FY27 (income-tax-only). Not enacted in the FY27 budget.

benchmark.source: CT OFA fiscal note on sSB-6 sec. 1 (File #705, 4/17/2026) - the identical $600/child, up-to-3-children refundable CTC

reforms.name: CT 2026 one-time tax rebate ($200/$400)
reforms.description: Gov. Lamont's proposed one-time $200/person ($400 joint) rebate for AGI under $200k/$400k (~1.6M taxpayers). OPM budgeted -$500.0M one-time in FY27. OPM's design includes a $320/$320k HoH tier and $200/$200k MFS tier - check the contrib parameterization covers them. Dropped from the adopted budget; the OPM estimate stands as the benchmark.

benchmark.source: CT OPM, Governor's FY2027 Midterm Adjustment Budget (2/4/2026), Refunds of Taxes line; corroborated by OFA's Synopsis of the Governor's Budget

reforms.name: ARPA 2021 CTC expansion (applied to 2024 data)
reforms.description: The ARPA $3,000/$3,600 fully-refundable CTC applied as a 2024-period reform and compared to JCT's TY2021 score (the FY21+FY22 sum, since advance payments and filing-season refunds straddle fiscal years). Three-year population/income vintage gap: 2024 incomes are higher (phase-outs bite more) and child counts slightly lower - an approximation band, not an exact target.

benchmark.source: JCT JCX-14-21 (3/9/2021), H.R.1319 as amended: Child Tax Credit improvements for 2021, FY21 -$25,826M + FY22 -$79,249M

reforms.name: ARPA 2021 childless EITC expansion (applied to 2024 data)
reforms.description: ARPA's one-year childless-EITC expansion (max ~$1,502, 15.3% phase-in/out, phase-out start $11,610, age 19+, 65 cap removed) applied at 2024 and compared to JCT's TY2021 score. All amounts are 2021 dollars applied to 2024 wage levels, which systematically shrinks the eligible range relative to the 2021 economy JCT scored - expect the model below the benchmark. Same vintage caveat as the ARPA CTC row.

benchmark.source: JCT JCX-14-21 (3/9/2021): strengthening the EITC for individuals with no qualifying children, total -$11,882M (nearly all FY2022)

reforms.name: CBO option — all individual rates +1pt (applied to 2024 data)
reforms.description: Raises all seven statutory rates on ordinary income by 1 percentage point. CBO/JCT scored $82.3B in FY2025 and $106.3B in FY2026 (first full year) on a pre-OBBBA baseline with TCJA rates in effect; applied here to 2024 law (also TCJA rates), so the comparison is same-rate-structure but different vintage - an approximation band.

benchmark.source: CBO, Options for Reducing the Deficit: 2025 to 2034 (Dec 2024), 'Increase Individual Income Tax Rates on Ordinary Income', alternative 1 (JCT staff estimate)

reforms.name: UBI mechanical check — $1,200/person/year
reforms.description: A flat $1,200/person/year universal basic income measured on the basic_income spending variable itself (not income_tax). The model total must equal weighted-person-mass x $1,200, so this row directly audits the dataset's calibrated person weights through the reform pathway - a UBI-shaped self-consistency check with an exact external anchor.

benchmark.source: Mechanical: Census PEP Vintage 2024 national resident population (340,110,988) x $1,200
